title: Verifier-Guided Evaluation of LLM-Generated Network Configurations: a Paired Study with Shared Initial Candidates
abstract: We preregistered and executed a paired confirmatory study (CAND-2026-001) that measured whether a verifier-triggered guarded pipeline (generate → validate → repair, ≤1 repair) reduces deterministic-invariant violations relative to single-shot initial generation for intent→configuration NetOps tasks. Using a deterministic synthetic task generator and a deterministic network verifier, we ran 200 preregistered tasks under shared_initial_candidate semantics with the hosted model gpt-5-mini (execution/model_configuration.json records temperature = null/unset). Baseline configurations passed the verifier in 199/200 tasks (99.5%); the guarded pipeline passed 200/200 (100%). Paired absolute risk difference (guarded − baseline) = 0.005; contingency counts n11=199, n10=1, n01=0, n00=0; exact two-sided McNemar p = 1.0; paired-bootstrap 95% percentile CI = [0.00, 0.015] (10,000 resamples, seed 1729). The single guarded improvement arose from one verifier-triggered repair that corrected a multi-step ordering violation. We report preregistration, full execution accounting (201 model calls: 200 shared initial + 1 repair), paired analysis, representative diagnostic artifacts, and bounded limitations grounded in the archived execution bundle.

sections.introduction:
Generative large language models (LLMs) are increasingly proposed to translate high-level operator intent into device configurations for network operations (NetOps). Operational correctness for such workflows requires generated configurations to satisfy deterministic invariants (reachability, policy compliance, ordering and workflow constraints, group-level safety). Prior work documents prototype intent→configuration systems and advocates verifier/validator stages, but artifact-grounded evidence quantifying generator→verifier→repair pipelines in a tightly controlled experimental design is limited [1],[2].

This study asks the preregistered research question: under shared_initial_candidate semantics—where exactly one sampled initial generation per task is deterministically reused by both baseline and guarded episodes—does permitting at most one verifier-triggered automated repair improve the per-task rate at which a deterministic verifier accepts generated configurations? Because the experiment enforced shared_initial_candidate semantics the estimand isolates the marginal effect of the verifier-triggered repair on an identical initial candidate (a repair-only effect); it does not measure the effect of independent guarded first-pass generations, constrained prompting, temperature tuning, or multi-sample selection.

Contributions. (1) A preregistered, fully archived paired experiment (CAND-2026-001) executing 200 intent→configuration tasks with a deterministic verifier and a hosted LLM (gpt-5-mini) under shared_initial_candidate semantics. (2) Complete execution accounting and deterministic reconciliation showing 200 shared initial generations and 1 repair call (201 model calls total). (3) Artifact-grounded confirmatory analysis reporting baseline pass 199/200 and guarded pass 200/200 with contingency counts (n11=199,n10=1,n01=0,n00=0), paired risk difference 0.005, exact two-sided McNemar p = 1.0, and bootstrap 95% CI = [0.00,0.015] (10,000 resamples, seed 1729). (4) A focused failure diagnosis for the single repaired pair using archived validator traces. (5) Detailed reproducibility guidance pointing to the archived execution bundle and deterministic reconciliation.
sections.related_work:
Prior NetOps and AIOps literature reports intent-driven configuration synthesis systems, prototype generator–validator pipelines, and curated evaluation suites that assess configuration generation accuracy under curated tasks [1],[2],[3]. Cross-domain work on generate→validate→repair in program repair and constrained synthesis motivates guarded pipelines: verifier-assisted repair often improves correctness when the oracle is well-specified [4],[5],[6]. Agentic-AI and LLM safety surveys emphasize hallucination/confabulation failure modes and recommend verifier gates, provenance, and constrained tool access for operational workflows [7],[8].

Synthesis and gap positioning. Most previous demonstrations either (a) evaluate first-pass generation accuracy across independent samples or (b) present software-engineering repair loops; few studies provide a preregistered paired design that reuses the identical initial candidate to isolate the repair-only effect. The supplied literature therefore motivates but does not itself answer whether a bounded verifier-triggered repair can reliably recover invariant compliance from an identical initial candidate in NetOps settings—our experiment directly addresses that narrower empirical gap.
sections.methodology:
Preregistration and estimand. The study was preregistered as CAND-2026-001 prior to observing outcomes. Primary estimand: paired_success_rate_difference_guarded_minus_baseline, the per-pair difference in the binary event that the deterministic verifier accepts the candidate (all encoded invariants pass). Generation semantics were fixed to shared_initial_candidate and each task produced exactly one initial model generation reused by both baseline and guarded episodes; the protocol allowed at most one automated repair call per task and specified a single confirmatory test (exact two-sided McNemar). The preregistration and experimental plan are archived and referenced in the execution manifest.

Task generation and selection. Tasks came from deterministic_netops_task_generator_v5 and were selected deterministically (the preregistration specifies the cycle/offset mapping used for ordinal selection). The task bank targets very_hard and extreme workflow patterns with multi-device ordering constraints, dependency rules, group invariants, and required per-task required_sequence fields. Each task manifest encodes initial_state, expected_final_state, required_sequence, allowed_touched_fields, and workflow policies; manifests are archived (execution/task_manifest.jsonl). Inclusion/exclusion rules (token-normalized leakage checks and syntactic pre-checks) were evaluated before model calls; the archived run shows no preregistered exclusions.

Model configuration and sampling semantics. The declared model in execution/model_configuration.json is gpt-5-mini and that file records temperature = null (unset). We explicitly state that temperature = null/unset in the archived configuration is not evidence of deterministic sampling or temperature = 0; hosted-model nondeterminism is therefore not excluded. The adapter hosted_netops_gvr_v1 enforced shared_initial_candidate semantics (one sampled initial generation per task deterministically reused by baseline and guarded episodes) and maximum_repair_calls_per_task = 1. Provider-call accounting in the execution manifest records model_calls_used = 201 with stage counts: shared_initial_generation = 200 and repair = 1.

Deterministic verifier and scoring rule. deterministic_netops_validator_v5 served as the oracle. The verifier performs deterministic parsing, per-device allowed-field checks, required_sequence ordering constraints, group invariants (e.g., at-least-one-up), and other dependency rules encoded in the task manifest. The binary scoring rule full_intent_constraint_validation returns 1 if all required invariants pass and 0 otherwise. The verifier emits per-episode validator traces (validation_before, validation_after) and violation codes; these traces are archived under execution/scoring/ and execution/responses/.

Paired experiment semantics and failed-call treatment. Because the experiment used shared_initial_candidate semantics, baseline and guarded episodes for a pair begin from the identical initial candidate; any difference in final per-pair acceptance can only arise from the permitted verifier-triggered repair (repair-only effect). The preregistered missingness plan treated persistent unparsable outputs as failures in sensitivity analyses; in the archived run there were no persistent unparsables.

Statistical analysis plan and exact-test details. The primary confirmatory test was the exact two-sided McNemar implementation applied to discordant counts n10 (guarded=1, baseline=0) and n01 (guarded=0, baseline=1). The executor computed the two-sided p by applying the binomial distribution with n = n10 + n01 under H0: p=0.5 and forming ptwo = 2 * min{BinomialCDF(k; n, 0.5), 1 - BinomialCDF(k - 1; n, 0.5)}; for our observed discordants (n = 1 with k = n10 = 1) this yields p = 2 * min{0.5, 0.5} = 1.0 (the analysis artifacts show p = 1.0). Paired-bootstrap percentile CIs for the risk difference were computed with 10,000 resamples using seed 1729 (bootstrap parameters recorded in analysis_log.jsonl).

Reproducibility guarantees. All runtime parameters (declared model, requested model, maximum_attempts_per_call, and the adapter's stage counts), per-call provider traces, task manifests, verifier traces, and analysis artifacts are archived in the execution bundle. The execution manifest indexes these artifacts and the deterministic_reconciliation JSON records provider-call stage counts and pair accounting. Reanalysis is reproducible by running the archived paired_binary_analysis_v1 executor on execution/raw_results.jsonl using the archived analysis configuration.
sections.results:
Execution accounting and deterministic reconciliation. The execution manifest reports started_at_utc = 2026-09-01T16:03:05.491039+00:00, completed_at_utc = 2026-09-01T16:32:13.298536+00:00, planned_episode_count = 400, completed_episode_count = 400, failed_episode_count = 0, and model_calls_used = 201. Deterministic_reconciliation confirms complete_pair_count = 200 and consistent pair accounting. Provider-call audit stage counts are shared_initial_generation = 200 and repair = 1.

Primary confirmatory outcome (artifact-grounded). The analysis/condition_summary.csv artifact shows:
- Baseline: successes = 199, failures = 1, observed = 200, success_rate = 0.995.
- Guarded: successes = 200, failures = 0, observed = 200, success_rate = 1.000.
The paired contingency artifact analysis/paired_contingency_table.csv records counts n11 = 199, n10 = 1, n01 = 0, n00 = 0. The paired absolute risk difference (guarded − baseline) = 0.005. The preregistered exact two-sided McNemar reported p = 1.0 for the observed discordant pattern and the paired-bootstrap percentile 95% CI for the risk difference (10,000 resamples, seed 1729) is [0.00, 0.015]. All these numeric values are exact matches to archived analysis artifacts (analysis/results.json, analysis/*.csv, analysis_log.jsonl).

Repair activity and representative diagnostics. The guarded pipeline invoked a single automated repair (repair stage count = 1). The archived validator_trace for the repaired pair identifies the failure as a multi-step ordering/workflow violation relative to the task's required_sequence (the task manifest encodes required_sequence with explicit ordered operations). The repair applied a small reordering patch that restored required ordering and satisfied group invariants; post-repair the verifier returned valid = true. Representative artifacts for this repaired pair are archived (execution/responses/task-000008-*, execution/scoring/task-000008-*), and the per-episode validator trace contains parsed_command_count, required_command_count, observed_touched_field_count, and violation_codes for both before/after states.

Missingness, exclusions, and contamination monitoring. The run recorded no excluded preregistered tasks and no missing pairs: complete_pairs = 200, baseline_only_observed_pairs = 0, guarded_only_observed_pairs = 0, both_missing_pairs = 0. The contamination_summary CSV in analysis artifacts contains no flagged entries. The deterministic_reconciliation provider-call audit shows hosted_model_call_event_count = 201, cache_hit_count = 0, cache_miss_count = 201, and stage_counts indicating the single repair.

Exploratory descriptive diagnostics. The archived task manifests and validator traces permit exploratory breakdowns by difficulty pattern (very_hard vs extreme), required_command_count, and changed_interface_count. In the archived sample the single failed baseline episode (the repaired case) occurred on an extreme/very_hard composite with required_command_count = 9 and changed_interface_count = 3, consistent with the preregistered hypothesis that multi-device policy interactions and ordering constraints concentrate failure risk. A companion artifact (analysis/paired_difference_figure.svg) visualizes the per-condition rates and bootstrap distribution used for CI construction.
sections.discussion:
Interpreting the paired estimand under shared_initial_candidate semantics. Because baseline and guarded conditions began from the identical initial candidate for every task, the observed paired difference isolates the marginal effect of permitting at most one verifier-triggered repair on that identical candidate (a repair-only effect). This estimand does not capture benefits that could arise from alternative guarded designs (independently prompted guarded generations, constrained prompting, temperature modulation, or mult-sample selection); separate preregistered contrasts would be required to estimate those different interventions.

Statistical power, discrete inference regime, and practical meaning. The preregistration targeted detection of ≈10–15 percentage-point paired improvements at N = 200 under baseline assumptions ~45–65% success. The observed baseline pass rate (199/200 = 99.5%) greatly exceeded those planning assumptions, producing low realized power to detect small absolute differences and putting the inference into a discrete regime where discordant counts are small integers. In this regime the exact two-sided McNemar p can be noninformative for rare discordant outcomes (our executor returned p = 1.0 for n = 1 discordant), so the paired-bootstrap CI [0.00, 0.015] is particularly useful to bound plausible effect sizes compatible with the data.

Operational implications and scope. The single repaired failure was a multi-device ordering breach; in this synthetic deterministic setting one narrowly scoped repair restored invariant compliance. This supports a constrained conclusion: verifier-guarded repair can correct certain localized ordering faults on identical initial candidates in a deterministic synthetic setting. It does not imply that verifier-guarded repair will correct semantic misinterpretations of intent, omissions only observable in live dataplane telemetry, or adversarially poisoned retrievals.

Threats to validity. Internal validity: shared_initial_candidate semantics and single initial generation per task limit conclusions to repair effects only. Construct validity: the deterministic verifier checks encoded invariants but does not emulate live dataplane behavior or runtime telemetry; some operational risks require live execution tests. External validity: a single model (gpt-5-mini) and a synthetic deterministic task bank constrain generalizability; multi-model and live-device studies are necessary to claim broader operational utility. Conclusion validity: the small number of discordant pairs implies large sampling uncertainty for small absolute effects; the bootstrap CI quantifies this uncertainty.

Reproducibility and archival guidance. All execution, provider-call traces, task manifests, verifier traces, and analysis artifacts are archived within the execution bundle and indexed by the execution manifest and deterministic_reconciliation.json (these files list the artifact filenames and the executor records). The analysis artifacts referenced (analysis/condition_summary.csv, analysis/paired_contingency_table.csv, analysis/paired_difference_figure.svg, analysis_log.jsonl) contain the exact numeric inputs used for inference. Reanalysis directions: run the archived paired_binary_analysis_v1 executor on execution/raw_results.jsonl with the archived analysis configuration (bootstrap_seed = 1729, resamples = 10000) to reproduce the reported bootstrap CI. The execution manifest records model_calls_used = 201 and stage_counts showing 200 shared initial generations and 1 repair; these counts are the authoritative accounting for the run.

Recommended next steps grounded in the artifacts. To increase operational relevance and answer broader open questions, future preregistered studies should (1) adopt independent first-pass generation semantics to measure guarded-prompt/ constrained-prompt effects, (2) test multiple models to assess cross-model generality beyond gpt-5-mini, (3) expand task diversity and include live-device telemetry or emulation checks, and (4) include adversarial contamination/poisoning experiments. Each recommendation follows directly from limitations observed in the archived run (single model, synthetic tasks, shared_initial_candidate semantics, limited adversarial testing).
sections.conclusion: We executed a preregistered paired experiment that measured the marginal effect of a verifier-triggered repair under shared_initial_candidate semantics for LLM-generated network configurations. In this synthetic deterministic task set using gpt-5-mini, baseline verifier acceptance was 199/200 and guarded acceptance was 200/200; a single automated repair corrected a multi-device ordering violation. The paired absolute risk difference was 0.005 with a paired-bootstrap 95% CI [0.00, 0.015] (10,000 resamples, seed 1729); the exact two-sided McNemar p = 1.0 for the single discordant pair. Artifact-grounded evidence supports a constrained conclusion: verifier-guarded repair can correct localized ordering faults in this synthetic setting, but broader operational claims require larger, multi-model, adversarial, and live-device studies. All execution, verifier, and analysis artifacts supporting these results are archived and indexed by the execution manifest.

disclosure_statement: Disclosure: This run implemented preregistered study CAND-2026-001 and was executed autonomously after the autonomy lock. Declared model: gpt-5-mini (execution/model_configuration.json records temperature = null/unset; null/unset is not evidence of deterministic sampling or temperature = 0). Orchestration adapter: hosted_netops_gvr_v1. Exact initial master prompt archived at provenance/master_prompt.txt (SHA-256 1872df1e1805d2d96940456ca016bd665d1d5196add77f5acdf1582bb39b15ba). Preregistration fixed generation_semantics = shared_initial_candidate (one sampled initial generation per task was deterministically reused by baseline and guarded episodes) and allowed at most one automated repair call per task. Model-call accounting in the archived execution manifest reflects 200 shared initial generation calls and 1 repair call (201 model calls total). The deterministic verifier used was deterministic_netops_validator_v5. Humans selected the broad topic family and constrained the initial master prompt prior to the autonomy lock as permitted by the track; no human manually edited technical manuscript content after the autonomy lock. All provider traces, verifier logs, task manifests, model-configuration records, and analysis artifacts are archived in the execution bundle and indexed by the execution manifest.
limitations: Synthetic deterministic task bank and verifier: results reflect correctness under the chosen synthetic intent templates and deterministic verifier and do not guarantee similar performance on live heterogeneous production devices or telemetry.
Single-model experiment (gpt-5-mini): findings do not demonstrate multi-model generality.

Shared_initial_candidate semantics: baseline and guarded conditions began from the same initial generation; the study measures verifier/repair effects only and does not evaluate independent first-pass generation contrasts.
Limited adversarial/contamination testing: the run did not include systematic adversarial retrieval or poisoned-context attacks; such threats remain an open evaluation axis.

Oracle coverage: the deterministic verifier enforces encoded invariants but may omit runtime behaviors and device-specific semantics observable only through live execution; external validity to live deployments is therefore limited.
